target_customer: Takeout and delivery diners wanting affordable fresh meals; the company planned to own and operate its robotic units (reported unit price just above $500,000 per auto-kitchen).
problem: Healthy restaurant meals cost $10 or more and restaurant labor, rent and overhead are high. Mezli built shipping-container restaurants where a robot assembles meals from ingredients prepped by a central kitchen.
business_model: Company-operated autonomous restaurants selling meals (takeout and delivery), with a possible later model of selling units

exit.reason: The company site describes the company in past tense and says it wound down in 2023 after a planned Series A did not close (read through a page-fetch summary of mezli.com).

technical_complexity.rationale: A three-person team had to build a food-safe robotic kitchen in a container with ingredient cartridges and control software; it opened a first unit in Mission Bay in August 2022.

defensibility.rationale: Hardware and operating know-how took time to copy, but no sourced patents, data or network effects; the unit economics rested on a roughly $500,000 per unit build.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: No source shows an incumbent copying or buying Mezli. A search result noted Sweetgreen bought robotic restaurant Spyce in August 2021, showing incumbent interest in the wedge.

market_need_then: Founders cited the cost of healthy takeout (about $10 or more) as the pain; TechCrunch (Nov 2021) framed the model against restaurant labor, overhead and real estate costs. No demand metrics found beyond about 10,000 meals served in fall 2022 per the company site.

branding.domain_note: Used mezli.com; no acquisition story found.

identity.visual_style: Shipping-container auto-kitchen; Mediterranean grain bowl menu
identity.voice_and_tone: Plain, cost-focused pitch (cheaper fresh food made by machine)

rebrands.why: Company site says it began in 2020 as EveryMeal; reason and date not given

branding.community_and_virality: Launch coverage in CNBC, Eater SF, Fox Business, TechCrunch and others (2021 to 2022). No evidence of community or merch.

brand_strength.rationale: Good launch press for a robot restaurant, but a trademark application for MEZLI (filed June 2021) is listed as dead and no sourced brand following exists.

outcome_analysis: Mezli raised a $3M seed in November 2021, opened its first autonomous restaurant at Spark Social in Mission Bay in August 2022 and served about 10,000 meals that fall. According to the company site it wound down in 2023 when its planned Series A did not close. A capital-heavy hardware model with a reported $500,000 plus unit cost and a thin funding history left no room to continue once the next round failed.
notes: Pre-seed of $125K (April 2021) rests on a single database (BounceWatch). CB Insights total of $3.13M over 2 rounds is consistent with the two rounds. Restaurant Technology News (2022) says a $3.5M seed in June, which conflicts with the TechCrunch $3M; recorded the TechCrunch figure. Shutdown details come from a page-fetch summary of mezli.com, not an independent post-mortem. No dated competitors found: TechCrunch named none and the competitor lists seen were undated aggregators (CB Insights, Owler).
